title: Penguins’ Sidney Crosby to miss at least 4 weeks after sustaining injury at Olympics
content:
The lower-body injury that kept Sidney Crosby out of the men’s hockey gold medal game at the Olympics will sideline him for at least the next four weeks, the Pittsburgh Penguins announced Wednesday.

Crosby was placed on injured reserve after returning to Pittsburgh from Milan earlier in the week.

Losing the 38-year-old captain for a critical stretch in the season is a big blow for the Penguins, who have a five-point cushion on the playoff cutoff line coming out of the Olympic break. They are seeking to return to the postseason for the first time since 2022 and are scheduled to play 15 games over the next four weeks as part of a compressed post-Olympic NHL schedule.

Crosby told reporters at practice Wednesday that he’s feeling good and trying to figure out how to return as soon as he can. He said he’s confident others on the team will step up while he’s out.

“To get to where we are at this point, it’s because of our team play. I don’t think it’s been because of any one person. It’s because collectively as a group, we’ve found different ways to win and different guys have stepped up. As long as we continue that and understand that, then I think we give ourselves a good chance.”

Crosby was injured while playing for Team Canada on Feb. 18 during a quarterfinal game against the Czech Republic. He endured two heavy hits on one shift from Czech defenseman Radko Gudas, including one where his legs spread awkwardly under the weight of the collision, before departing for the dressing room.

Crosby skated twice more at closed practices in Milan while trying to get himself in a position to return during the tournament. Ultimately, he made the call to miss Sunday’s gold medal game, watching Team USA beat Canada 2-1 in overtime.

He said Wednesday he was closer to playing in the gold medal game than he thought he would be, but ultimately couldn’t. At the time, he was focused, he said, on playing in that game, and not on how playing would affect the Penguins’ season.

“That’s not any disrespect to our team or what I feel about this season, or anything like that. We all put a lot of work in to try to be as successful as possible here. But given the opportunity to play in the Olympics and in that game, I think trying to play was all my focus was on.”

Crosby has 27 goals and 59 points in 56 games for Pittsburgh this season — putting him on pace to extend his record-setting run of point-per-game campaigns to 21.
